title: Shoulder dystocia
stem: Delivery room in the ED. A woman at term is delivering on the trolley before the obstetric team arrives. The head has delivered but it has pulled back tight against the perineum, and the next push does not deliver the shoulders. A midwife and a nurse are with you. Manage the delivery on the manikin.
notes:
Checked against RCOG Green-top Guideline 42 (Shoulder dystocia, 2012, reviewed) and the ALSO (HELPERR) course.

Recognise: the 'turtle sign' (the head retracts against the perineum) and failure of routine axial traction. State 'shoulder dystocia' aloud, call for help, note the time the head delivered. Avoid excessive or downward traction, fundal pressure and pulling on the neck.

First: McRoberts (hyperflex the hips, thighs to the abdomen) with suprapubic pressure over the posterior aspect of the anterior shoulder (continuous, then rocking) — resolves most cases. Then internal manoeuvres or delivery of the posterior arm (RCOG gives no fixed order); rotational manoeuvres: Rubin II (behind the anterior shoulder), Woods' screw (in front of the posterior shoulder), reverse Woods'. All-fours (Gaskin) is an alternative, especially without an epidural. Third-line: deliberate clavicle fracture, Zavanelli (cephalic replacement), symphysiotomy.

Your notes use HELPERR, which matches ALSO. Difference: episiotomy is not needed in every case; RCOG uses it only to make room for internal manoeuvres. Document times and manoeuvres; debrief; paediatric review for brachial plexus injury.

steps.label: Talk to the midwife
steps.hint: Name it, call for help, note the time, stop pushing.

opts.t: 'This is a shoulder dystocia.' Call obstetrics, neonatology and anaesthetics; note the time of head delivery
opts.mark: States shoulder dystocia, calls for help, notes the time

opts.t: Ask her to stop pushing for now

opts.r: Excessive traction causes brachial plexus injury.

opts.t: Push on the top of the uterus
opts.r: Fundal pressure worsens impaction and risks uterine rupture.

steps.label: Manoeuvres
steps.hint: McRoberts + suprapubic pressure; then posterior arm or rotation; then all-fours.

opts.t: McRoberts: lie her flat, two helpers hyperflex her hips, thighs onto the abdomen
Suprapubic pressure from the side of the fetal back, over the anterior shoulder, continuous then rocking, with gentle axial traction
opts.mark: Suprapubic pressure from the fetal back side

opts.t: Still stuck: hand in posteriorly; deliver the posterior arm by flexing the elbow and sweeping across the chest
Or rotate: pressure behind the anterior shoulder (Rubin II) and in front of the posterior shoulder (Woods' screw)
Shoulders deliver; baby to the resuscitaire; note the time
opts.mark: Delivers and hands the baby for neonatal assessment
opts.r: The baby is floppy at first, then cries after inflation breaths. Head-to-body interval 3 minutes.

opts.t: Routine large episiotomy before anything else
opts.r: Shoulder dystocia is a bony problem. Episiotomy only to make room for internal manoeuvres.

steps.label: After the birth
steps.hint: Watch for PPH and tears; document; baby review; debrief.

opts.t: Anticipate PPH and perineal tears; active third stage
Document times, manoeuvres, who was present, which shoulder was anterior
Paediatric review for brachial plexus injury and fractures; debrief the parents

qs.a: The born head pulls back against the perineum
wrong: Swelling of the maternal neck veins
A sudden fetal bradycardia on the CTG after the head

qs.a: Behind the anterior shoulder, from the fetal back
wrong: On the fundus, pushing down with each contraction
On the perineum, supporting the head
Over the maternal sacrum, from behind
Forceps rotation of the fetal head

badge.name: Shoulder Shrug
badge.flavor: Say it, call, McRoberts plus pressure. Never pull or push the fundus.

cards.why: Straightens the sacrum and rotates the symphysis.

cards.q: Is episiotomy mandatory in shoulder dystocia?
options: No — only to allow internal manoeuvres
Yes, a large episiotomy is always the first step
To the anterior aspect of the posterior shoulder
To the posterior aspect of the anterior shoulder
To the fetal head during traction
To the maternal abdomen above the pubis

cards.why: Also maternal diabetes, obesity, previous dystocia.

cards.q: What must be recorded after shoulder dystocia?
options: Apgar scores and the cord gases only
Birth weight and length of the second stage
The time the midwife was called
